re-testudo-horsfieldii.title: Russian Tortoise
re-testudo-horsfieldii.summary: A hardy, active, burrowing tortoise from Central Asia. It can live 50 years or more, so it's a long-term commitment.
rows: 5–10 in shell length. Males are smaller
One adult: 7 × 3.5 ft floor space (24.5 sq ft) minimum, or an outdoor pen when the weather allows. Juveniles under about 6 in can use 4 × 2 ft temporarily. Add 10 sq ft for each extra tortoise
Always provide a humid hide with damp substrate. Juvenile enclosures should be 40–75%
Strong UVB is required, plus bright daylight lighting. Lights on about 14 h in summer and 10 h in winter
High-fiber, low-protein, low-sugar: leafy greens, grasses and edible weeds such as dandelion and clover. Not grocery vegetables or fruit as a staple. Feed on a plate
Most dislike handling. Scoop up from below with both hands and support the body. Wash hands before and after
Active by day and loves to dig. Give 4–6 in of loose sand and soil substrate
Central Asia (dry steppe and rocky desert)
notes: Not a social species, so it's fine kept alone. Don't house males together.
warn: Lives 50+ years and needs far more floor space than most tanks provide.
